shortDescription.text: Private key material must never be in source control. Deleting it later doesn't remove it from history.

help.text: Treat the key as compromised: generate a new pair, install the new public key or certificate wherever the old one is trusted, then remove the old one. Keep private keys in a secret manager or key vault.

shortDescription.text: An AWS access key ID is half of a usable credential and names the account it belongs to.

help.text: Deactivate, then delete, the access key in IAM and check CloudTrail for its use. Prefer short-lived credentials: IAM roles, or OIDC federation from CI.

shortDescription.text: An AWS secret access key grants everything its user or role can do.

help.text: Deactivate, then delete, the access key in IAM and check CloudTrail for its use. Prefer short-lived credentials: IAM roles, or OIDC federation from CI.

shortDescription.text: A storage account shared key grants full control of the account and can't be scoped.

help.text: Regenerate the key on the storage account (the two keys can be rotated one at a time without downtime) and update its consumers. Prefer Microsoft Entra ID authorization, and disable shared key access where nothing needs it.

shortDescription.text: A SAS token is a bearer credential. Anyone holding the URL has its access until it expires.

help.text: Revoke it: delete or change the stored access policy it uses, or rotate the account key that signed it. Prefer short-lived user delegation SAS issued at run time.

shortDescription.text: An Entra ID client secret lets anyone authenticate as the application.

help.text: Delete the secret from the app registration, check the service principal's sign-in logs, and move to a managed identity or workload identity federation where possible.

shortDescription.text: A password inside a connection string is a live database credential.

help.text: Change the password on the database, then load the connection string from configuration (a Key Vault reference, an environment variable) or use managed identity authentication.

shortDescription.text: Credentials inside a URL leak into logs, shell history and error messages.

help.text: Change the password, and pass credentials separately from the URL: an environment variable, a secret store or a credential helper.

shortDescription.text: A GitHub token can read or write repositories and act as its owner.

help.text: Revoke the token (the owner's developer settings, or the organization's token settings), review the audit log for its use, and replace it with a GitHub App or the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN where possible.

shortDescription.text: A GitLab personal access token acts as its owner across the instance.

help.text: Revoke it in the owner's access token settings, review the audit events, and replace it with a project or group token that has an expiry date.

shortDescription.text: A Slack token grants workspace access as a bot or user.

help.text: Revoke it (Slack's auth.revoke method, or the app's OAuth settings) and keep the replacement in a secret store.

shortDescription.text: A Slack webhook URL lets anyone post into the channel as the integration.

help.text: Remove the webhook in the Slack app's Incoming Webhooks settings, create a new one, and keep it in a secret store.

shortDescription.text: A live Stripe secret or restricted key can move real money.

help.text: Roll the key in the Stripe Dashboard, review the API request logs for its use, and prefer restricted keys with only the permissions needed.

shortDescription.text: A Google API key is billed to its project and often has no usage restrictions.

help.text: Delete or regenerate the key on the Google Cloud console's Credentials page, and restrict its replacement to the APIs and applications that need it.

shortDescription.text: An npm token can publish packages as its owner: a direct supply-chain risk.

help.text: Revoke it (npm token revoke, or the Access Tokens page), check recent versions of the owner's packages, and publish from CI with trusted publishing or a granular token.

shortDescription.text: An Anthropic API key is billed to its organization and can read its workspace data.

help.text: Delete the key in the Anthropic console, check the workspace's usage for activity you don't expect, and issue a replacement held in a secret store.

shortDescription.text: An OpenAI API key is billed to its organization and can read its project data.

help.text: Delete the key on the OpenAI platform's API keys page, check usage for activity you don't expect, and issue a replacement held in a secret store.

shortDescription.text: A secret assigned inline as a literal is almost always a real one pasted in.

help.text: If it's a real credential, rotate it where it was issued and load it from the environment or a secret store. If it's test or example data, add an allow entry with the reason.

shortDescription.text: Dotenv files hold real environment secrets. Commit a .env.example with placeholders instead.

help.text: Stop tracking it (git rm --cached), add it to .gitignore, rotate every secret it held, and commit a .env.example with placeholders instead.

shortDescription.text: Terraform state stores resource attributes in plain text, including generated passwords and keys. Use a remote backend.

help.text: Stop tracking it, rotate the secrets it contains, and move state to a remote backend with encryption and restricted access.

shortDescription.text: Key stores, certificate bundles and SSH identity files usually contain private keys.

help.text: Stop tracking it, replace the keys it holds, and keep key stores in a secret manager or key vault.
